v4.9.080 - the safety net, not the app (#364, #365, #366, #367)

NOTHING IN THIS CHANGES WHAT THE APP DOES. #363 - the page staying where you put
it - is already on the devices. What follows is what was learned chasing the
random day, the tests that now hold it, and two places where the app was too
quiet to be diagnosed.

WHAT WAS CHASED, AND WHAT IT TURNED OUT TO BE

#364 The random day had failed on three seeds, always the same shape: after one
     device had been away, the two ended with the frames in different orders.
     Written down small - two devices rearranging while apart, then both writing
     AND rearranging and coming back together - it passes every time.

     Then the day was given a watching mode (FH_WATCH=1) that stops at the first
     step the two will not agree on. It stopped at step three, and a test doing
     exactly what step three does passes on its own. The window was too short.
     With a fair one, the frames converge at every step of the day.

     So the frame orders were never wrong. My watcher was.

#365 With the frames cleared, the day failed on a SETUP instead: one device had
     two of the three made, the other had one. Written down small - one device
     makes a setup while the other is away - it failed every time.

     And the setup was not lost either. The device that had been away simply
     stopped asking. The app listens only while its window is in front AND it has
     been touched in the last ten seconds, which is deliberate and reasonable -
     but a desktop sitting behind another window hears nothing at all, and to the
     person that looks exactly like work disappearing.

     Two places were too quiet to tell these apart, and both now speak:
       - a pull says WHICH settings arrived, by name. "It never came" and "it came
         and was thrown away" are different faults and looked identical.
       - a heartbeat that looks and finds nothing says so, once every twenty
         seconds. A device that has gone deaf and a device with genuinely nothing
         to fetch both said nothing at all. That cost an hour.

#366 WRITTEN, NOT SHIPPED. Roman's rule: a device nobody is looking at has no
     reason to be kept up to date, but the moment somebody touches it - or just
     scrolls - it should catch up, with no button and no particular action.

     Switched on, the setups test goes from failing after ninety seconds to
     passing in twenty-two. It also broke two things the suite had proven: a card
     stopped showing the version just drawn on, and a device was slower to take
     the other's writing. The extra pull lands in moments the app is not ready
     for. That is the next piece of work, and it is the same family as #352 and
     #356 - a pull still touching what is in front of you. The rule goes in
     behind it.

#367 Every run has a number now. FH_RUN=<n> goes at the front of the command and
     is written as the first line of the log, so a "zzz" can be matched to the
     run that produced it instead of guessed at.

THE SIMULATOR

  - a nudge brings that window to the front first. Two browser windows cannot
    both be in front, so nudging a background one left it correctly ignoring us
    and made it look as though work had been lost.
  - seven new tests: two devices rearranging apart; both writing and rearranging
    and returning together; two writing seconds apart while online; a setup made
    while the other is away; and the three scribble ones from #361.

26 of 27 pass. The one failure is the setups test, which is precisely the one
that needs #366 - so the split is clean and the next step is obvious.
